山东: 中国东部的沿海省份。看中国地图时，山东有一块半岛伸进黄海；北京在它的西北方向，上海在它的南边。
Shandong: A coastal province in eastern China. On a map, its peninsula reaches into the Yellow Sea; Beijing is northwest of it, and Shanghai is farther south.
army: A large group of soldiers who serve and fight together.
cavalry: Soldiers who fight while riding horses.
Central Plains: The old farming heartland of northern China.
Bianzhong: A set of ancient Chinese bronze bells hung on a frame and played like an orchestra.
Bo Ya: A famous qin player from an old Chinese story.
Bai Juyi: A famous Chinese poet who lived about 1,200 years ago.
Cao Cao: A powerful Three Kingdoms leader whom people still argue about today.
Cloth-Bag Monk: A cheerful wandering monk whom many Chinese people connect with the smiling big-bellied image of Maitreya.
Daiyu: A short form of Lin Daiyu's name.
Dao De Jing: A short classic linked to Laozi that talks about living with the natural way of the world.
Du Fu: A famous Chinese poet who cared deeply about ordinary people and hard times.
Dunhuang: A famous place in northwestern China known for its cave murals.
Eight Immortals: A famous group of Daoist immortals in Chinese stories, each with a different personality and background.
Emperor Huizong: A Song dynasty emperor named Zhao Ji who was famous for painting birds and flowers.
Feitian: Flying heavenly figures often seen in Dunhuang murals.
Guanyin: A compassionate Buddhist figure who often helps people in Chinese stories.
cobalt: A mineral that can turn bright blue in very high heat.
Eastern Han dynasty: The later part of the Han dynasty, about 2,000 years ago.
Eastern Jin dynasty: A time when part of China was ruled from the south, about 1,700 years ago.
Five Dynasties period: A short, unsettled time after the Tang dynasty when rulers changed quickly.
Guan Di temples: Temples where people honor Guan Yu as Lord Guan.
Guan Yu: A famous Three Kingdoms hero remembered for loyalty and a long green-bladed weapon in later stories.
Han dynasty: A powerful time in China more than 2,000 years ago.
halberd: A long weapon with a spear point and a blade on it.
Himalayas: The huge mountain range that includes Mount Everest.
Jia Baoyu: The unusual young main character of Dream of the Red Chamber, who loves poetry and beauty more than official success.
Jiangnan: The warm, watery region south of the Yangtze River.
Jade Emperor: The ruler of Heaven in many Chinese myths and stories.
Jingdezhen: The Chinese town most famous for making porcelain.
Jingdezhen Ceramic University: A university in Jingdezhen where many students study ceramics and porcelain making.
Jingdezhen China Ceramics Museum: A museum in Jingdezhen where visitors can see many famous Chinese ceramic works.
Jingwei: A small myth bird that keeps carrying stones and twigs to fill the sea.
khan: A title used by rulers in parts of Central and East Asia.
Kuafu: A giant from an old Chinese myth who ran after the sun.
Laozi: An ancient Chinese thinker linked with the Dao De Jing and early Daoist ideas.
Lin Chong: A major Water Margin hero who is pushed into outlaw life after repeated traps and injustice.
Lin Daiyu: One of the most memorable girls in Dream of the Red Chamber, known for poetry, sensitivity, and the flower-burial scene.
kaolin: A very pure white clay used to make porcelain.
Li Bai: A famous Chinese poet known for moonlight, travel, and bold imagination.
Li Qingzhao: One of China's most famous women poets, known for writing both lively and sorrowful song lyrics.
Liu Bei: A major Three Kingdoms leader remembered for kindness and persistence.
Ming dynasty: A time in China from 1368 to 1644.
Maitreya: A Buddhist figure linked in China with the smiling big-bellied monk often seen near temple entrances.
Northern and Southern Dynasties: A long time when northern and southern China often had different rulers.
Northern Dynasties: A time about 1,500 years ago when several dynasties ruled northern China.
Northern Wei period: A northern Chinese dynasty about 1,500 years ago.
Nuwa: A goddess in ancient Chinese myth who repaired the broken sky.
Qin: One of the old states that later united China.
Qin Shihuang: The first emperor of a united China, who lived more than 2,000 years ago.
Qin dynasty: China's first united empire, started by Qin Shi Huang more than 2,000 years ago.
Qing dynasty: China's last imperial dynasty, from 1644 to 1912.
Qinghai-Tibet Plateau: A very high land area in western China, sometimes called the roof of the world.
Shang dynasty: A very early Chinese dynasty more than 3,000 years ago.
Sogdians: An Iranian-speaking people of ancient Central Asia whose trade networks linked many cities along the Silk Roads.
Son of Heaven: An old title for the person who ruled an empire in China.
Song dynasty: A time in China about 1,000 years ago.
Song Jiang: A central Water Margin figure who wants to stay loyal yet is drawn into leading Liangshan.
Su Shi: A famous Song dynasty writer and poet who is also called Su Dongpo.
Sui dynasty: A short dynasty about 1,400 years ago that helped start the imperial exam system.
Spring and Autumn period: An early time in Chinese history when many states competed for power.
Tang dynasty: A powerful and creative time in China about 1,300 years ago.
White Horse Temple: A famous temple in Luoyang that many people connect with the early story of Buddhism coming to China.
Xuanzang: The real monk whose westward journey later inspired Tang Monk in Journey to the West.
Xi'an: A major old Chinese city where the Terracotta Warriors were found nearby.
Xin Qiji: A Song dynasty poet who also had real military experience and wrote powerful emotional lyrics.
Wei and Jin periods: A time about 1,700 years ago when a few powerful families had a lot of influence.
Wang Xizhi: A famous Chinese calligrapher who lived about 1,700 years ago.
Warring States period: A time more than 2,000 years ago when several states fought to rule China.
Yellow River: A great river in northern China and one of the longest rivers in the world.
Xue Baochai: An important girl in Dream of the Red Chamber, often remembered for calm good sense and steadiness.
Xia dynasty: The dynasty that later stories describe as China's earliest kingdom.
Xiongnu: A horse-riding people from the northern grasslands.
Xianbei: A group of peoples who lived across the northern grasslands and northern China.
Yan Liang: A general from the Three Kingdoms stories and history.
Zhuge Liang: A famous Three Kingdoms strategist known for calm thinking and clever plans.
Zhong Ziqi: The friend in an old Chinese story who truly understood Bo Ya's music.
ruler: The leader of a country or kingdom, such as a king or emperor.
footbinding: The old practice of tightly wrapping girls' feet to change their shape and keep them small.
loom: A machine used to weave thread into cloth.
Abing: A famous erhu musician from Wuxi whose piece Moon Reflected on the Second Spring became very well known.
Mogao Caves: The famous painted cave temples near Dunhuang.
莫高窟: 敦煌附近最有名的石窟群，里面有很多壁画和彩塑。
飞天: 敦煌壁画里很有名的飞天形象，没有翅膀，却像在空中飞。
宋徽宗赵佶: 宋朝的一位皇帝，也很有名，因为他很会画花鸟。
秦始皇: 中国第一个统一大帝国的皇帝，生活在两千多年前。
西安: 中国一座很有名的古城，兵马俑就在附近被发现。
景德镇: 中国最有名的瓷器城市之一。
景德镇中国陶瓷博物馆: 景德镇的一座陶瓷博物馆，能看到很多有名的瓷器作品。
景德镇陶瓷大学: 景德镇的一所大学，很多学生在那里学习陶瓷和做瓷器。
粟特人: 生活在古代中亚、说伊朗语族语言的一群人；他们的商路连接了丝绸之路沿线许多城市。
